chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who performs Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj), who wishes to go out to al-Ta'if. He said: 'He should enter the state of Ihram for Hajj from Mecca, and I like that he does not go out from it except in the state of Ihram, and he should not pass through al-Ta'if, for it is close to Mea.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where Umrah is performed first, then Hajj)
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: In the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يُهِلُّ: To enter the state of Ihram by reciting the Talbiyah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim performing Tamattu' who travels to al-Ta'if?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadi' (AS) to clarify the miqat status for a Mutamatti' pilgrim traveling to al-Ta'if; since al-Ta'if is within the boundaries of Mecca's extended sacred precinct (Haram), the pilgrim does not exit the state of Ihram but remains consecrated for Hajj. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that proximity to Mecca determines whether a location serves as a new miqat or remains part of the existing sacred zone, ensuring the continuity of the Hajj ritual state.
